attachments.text:
Tanners Row Summer Run 10K - medical notes
Sunday 2 May 2027 / gun 10:00 / 60 runners / 10K
contact Samuel Adeyemi 555-0185
On-site ambulance cover is set out in the attached paperwork from Lifeline Event Medics.

FIRST AID
3 posts (start, finish, midpoint). 6 qualified first aiders. nowhere more than 1.5km from a post. 2 bike responders w/ defibs

WEATHER / WATER
water every 2.5k. forecast check -48h and -2h. >28C earlier start or shorter course. >32C cancel. foil + warm tent at finish if cold/wet

HOSPITAL
Port Halden General Hospital, 10km from finish. pickup point the top of Quay Street, route walked w/ first aiders. ED told date + numbers

race week email: dress for weather, carry phone if poss. most have run w/ us before. entrant list w/ emergency contacts kept at start

COMMS
radios on medical channel at all posts + bikes, phones backup. amb calls go via medical lead, who gives crew the barrier to come to

LEAD
Patrick Doyle, registered paramedic, on site from -1hr til last runner in. can withdraw any runner

attachments.name: race_plan.txt
attachments.text:
RACE PLAN
Tanners Row Summer Run 10K | Sunday 2 May 2027
Organiser: Tanners Row Business Association
Race director: Samuel Adeyemi
Reference: EV-91255

Overview
The Tanners Row Summer Run 10K is a 10K race of 10 km for 60 entrants, based in the Tanners Row area of Port Halden. The start is at 10:00 and the course closes at 12:00.

Course
The course runs in order along Quay Street, Kings Parkway, Albion Road, Cooper Street and Dyer Street, all of which are closed to traffic for the race. Major roads crossed: Queen's Road, Ferry Road and Cross Avenue. The finish is in Market Square.

Course dimensions
Survey widths: Quay Street 10 m, Cooper Street 16 m, Dyer Street 16 m, kerb to kerb, excluding footways. Start pens sit side by side across the full carriageway, and spectators have the pavement and a grassed verge along most of the route.

Support
Entrants collect numbers from the top of Quay Street from one hour before the start. Timing is by chip, with mats at the start and finish. Results are posted on the Tanners Row website the same day.

attachments.name: traffic_plan.txt
attachments.text:
TRAFFIC MANAGEMENT PLAN
Event: Tanners Row Summer Run 10K
Date: Sunday 2 May 2027
Applicant: Tanners Row Business Association
Prepared by: Halloway Road Management
Issue: 1.4

1. Scope
This plan describes how traffic will be managed for the Tanners Row Summer Run 10K, a 10K race in the Tanners Row area of Port Halden with a 10:00 start. It has been prepared to accompany the permit application and should be read with the race plan. See the attached correspondence from the police for the escort.

2. Road closures
Temporary closures will be in force as follows, with barriers and advance signing supplied by Pathfinder Road Crews.
- Quay Street, Tanner Street to Rope Walk: closed 08:30 to 12:30
- Kings Parkway, Canon Road to Salter Way: closed 08:30 to 12:30
- Albion Road, Rope Walk to Salter Way: closed 08:30 to 12:30
- Cooper Street, Tanner Street to Lamb Street: closed 08:30 to 12:30
- Dyer Street, Bridge Row to Rope Walk: closed 08:30 to 12:30

3. Major crossings
Each major crossing has its own control point, staffed from 08:30 until the last runner has passed.
- Queen's Road at Kings Parkway: 4 traffic marshals with stop/go boards, one supervisor
- Ferry Road at Cooper Street: 3 traffic marshals with stop/go boards, one supervisor
- Cross Avenue at Cooper Street: 2 traffic marshals with stop/go boards, one supervisor

4. Diversions
Signed diversions will operate for the duration of the closures.
- Quay Street: traffic diverted via Victoria Road and High Street, signed from Canon Road
- Kings Parkway: traffic diverted via Regent Road and Canal Road, signed from Bridge Row
- Albion Road: traffic diverted via Tram Street and Regent Road, signed from Salter Way
- Cooper Street: traffic diverted via High Street and Regent Road, signed from Rope Walk
- Dyer Street: traffic diverted via Church Road and High Street, signed from Lamb Street

5. Emergency vehicle access
A clear lane of at least 3.5 m will be kept along the closed section for emergency vehicles. Barrier staff hold radios on the event channel and can open any closure within two minutes on request from the event controller, who is in direct contact with the police and ambulance control rooms.

6. Notification
All frontages on the closed streets receive a letter drop 21 days before the event, with a further reminder at 7 days. Advance notice signs go up 10 days before, and bus operators have been given the closure times.

7. Reopening
A sweep vehicle follows the last runner. Closures are lifted in the order listed, after a barrier and litter check, with all roads open by 12:30.
